data.text/markdown:
Hurdle: the same question as Movers, answered by small trees

At 13:30 every day, for each stock: will it move by the end of the horizon (15:30) by at least THETA percent, and up or down? The Movers notebook answers with one TSMixer that reads the raw morning. This notebook answers the same question on the same stock-days, with the same labels, calls and scoring, using gradient-boosted trees on a short table of numbers. It is the control for the TSMixer: if trees on a few summaries cannot beat the activity rule, a network on the raw path has to show it can do more. The model is a hurdle, two small questions instead of one:
  1. Will it move? P(move): a yes / no tree trained on every stock-day
  2. Which way, if it moves? P(up | move): trained only on the stock-days that moved
Each day the K stocks with the highest P(move) are called, each long if P(up | move) is above one half, else short. A direct three-class tree (down / flat / up in one model) runs beside it as a control.
  • every stock-day counts once: the labels are classes, so a 5% move weighs as much as a 1% move
  • no search: the trees' knobs are fixed (shallow, slow, regularized); only the inputs change, in a handful of steps, and the best of those few is compared with the luck bar
  • two rules need no model: random picks, and the K stocks with the biggest average move over the last 20 days (the hurdle that every model has to clear)
  • a luck band: the labels shuffled inside each day, with the model's calls kept

Settings

The next cell holds every setting. Keep the first three blocks the same as in the Movers notebook and both notebooks score the same stock-days.
  1. The question: when the prediction is made, how far ahead it looks, what counts as a move
  2. The book: cash and the size of a position, which give the number of calls per day
  3. The stocks and the data: how many stocks, and three consecutive date ranges TRAIN → VALIDATION → TEST
  4. The inputs: the morning read before the decision, and the four input steps compared

The stocks

The screen looks at every stock with 1-minute bars since UNIVERSE_FROM, on the TRAIN days only: the share of days it moved at least THETA between the decision and the horizon's end, its typical move, price, and the dollars traded in that window. Stocks with gaps or under $1 million traded in the window are dropped; the most active UNIVERSE_N stay (Table 1). The result is saved in var/movers/ and shared with the Movers notebook.

data.text/markdown:
The data and the split

The 1-minute bars of every stock from TRAIN's first day to TEST's last, and every input built from them (tsmixer_lab.build, the same inputs as the TSMixer notebooks). Table 2 shows the days:
  • history only: the first 10 sessions, read for the typical sizes, never learned
  • TRAIN: the trees learn; its last 10 days are held out to choose the number of boosting rounds (the trees' early stopping)
  • VALIDATION: every input step is scored here; TEST: read once, at the very end
Table 3 counts the classes. A model that always says "flat" is right on the biggest class, which is why only the calls count.

data.text/markdown:
The hurdle: what needs no model

On each day the two rules call K stocks with a random side. A pick is right when the stock moved at least THETA the called way, which a random side gets half of the time it moved at all. Table 4 is the bar every model has to clear, on TRAIN and on VALIDATION:
  • random picks: any K stocks of the day
  • activity picks: the K stocks with the biggest average move over the last 20 days. No model, no training. A tree that only learned which stocks are active will tie it; only knowing something about today or the direction beats it

data.text/html: Table 4 · The hurdle: 5 calls a day, no model

data.text/markdown:
The input steps

Each row of Table 5 is one tree model (hurdle or direct) fit on the TRAIN days with one set of inputs, then asked for its K calls on every VALIDATION day. The columns:
  • excess z (vs activity): per day, the share of the model's calls that are right minus what the activity picks with a random side would get, averaged over days, divided by its standard error over days. It is 0 when the trees know what the activity rule knows and nothing more
  • shuffle z 97.5%: the same z when the labels are shuffled inside each day, the 97.5th percentile of that many shuffles. A row is above luck only if its z clears this, and the best row has to clear the bar for the best of all the rows (below Table 5)
  • dir right and dir p: among the picks that moved, the share called on the right side, and its p-value against a coin
  • rounds (and the held-out loss against "always the class shares"): how many boosting rounds the 10 held-out days chose

Best: + morning, hurdle. Excess z +0.61 over the activity rule; 615 calls over 123 days, 23.4% right against 22.3% for the activity rule. The best of 8 rows reaches z ≥ 2.73 by luck only 2.5% of the time → within luck: what the best of this many tries looks like by chance.
